newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Fabius says no higher taxes or spending.
newsitem.headline: France's Fabius says no higher taxes or spending.

text.p: Former Socialist prime minister Laurent Fabius said that if the French left won Sunday's runoff parliamentary election vote it would not raise taxes or spending to pay for its policies.
"On the one hand, there is no question of raising total public spending, secondly there is no question of raising taxes," Fabius said in an interview with France Inter radio.

"There is some reorienting to do, but taxes need to be lowered, not raised. I am being completely clear," he said. "It is true, there is certainly a problem with public finances because we have the feeling that, already, the accounts are in trouble."
The Socialists have pledged to create 700,000 new jobs in France, with 350,000 in the public sector, if they take control of the lower house National Assembly.
